classification.difficultyReason: Each equation needs terms collected from both sides into one side, then an HCF factorisation and the null factor law. Part a is scaffolded with its rearrangement and factorisation shown. Part b removes that scaffold and has a mixed-sign collection. The hardest part is c, where x - 3x^2 = 7x needs a rearrangement that is not signposted and reduces to -3x^2 - 6x = 0. The solver must then choose to factor out -3x and keep track of the negative sign. This is a little more than p6-q4-block, which only moves one term and factors an HCF. It is a little less than p12-q8, which needs trinomial factorisations and a fuller rearrangement to ax^2+bx+c=0. No new representation, interpretation or insight is needed.
